label: canon-flat-in12-n30
_why: THE FLAT-COST, LIFTED-RUNG-0 ARM (user-ruled 2026-09-10, after FINDINGS F108): the vanilla-1836 premise is DROPPED. Three changes from phase 2's book (canon-je24-a22): (1) rung 0's input value × 1.2 — the 1836 tier deliberately less profitable than vanilla so it dies when the ladder arrives — with the ladder anchored on the lifted rung 0 (rung k inputs = I0 × 1.2 × 1.5^k); (2) building_cost FLAT at the vanilla anchor on every rung (600 / 800 / 400), the §10.61 book, because F108 §6 found the stall rate tracks the cost ladder's steepness (flat-cost books 0 of 7 at 0.95–1.71× vanilla; ×2^k 8 of 46; ×2.5^k 3 of 3); (3) ai_value linear by era, 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000 / 4,000, in place of 1,000 × 3^era. Kept: A 2.2 / B 1.5 over vanilla's own methods, the 24-month industry bar, the §10.75 pool defines; the cost divisor is vanilla's 0.001 (the auto formula at flat cost). 30 × 1836 → 1936.1.1, timeout 420, no gate. Generated by `make_ab_config --A 2.2 --B 1.5 --in0 1.2 --cost-flat --ai-ladder 1000,2000,3000,4000 --ai-defines <the six>` + bar 24; dry-run build clean (lint, negative goods, solvency, tech content, start conversion, preflight).

_delta: vs phase 2 (canon-je24-a22, 10 runs): rung-0 inputs (×1.2, ladder anchored on it), building_cost (flat vs ×2.2^k), ai_value (linear vs 3^era), cost divisor (0.001 vs 0.000125). vs vanilla: the whole mod; 1836 is no longer vanilla by construction — every rung-0 building starts with 20% dearer inputs.

_predictions.P1_stalls: At most 1 stall (< 0.70× the vanilla mean) in 30 and at most 3 runs below 0.80× — the flat-cost books read 0 of 7; a rate at phase 1's 20% would say the cost ladder was not the cause.
_predictions.P2_rung0_dies: The oldest rung's tiered workforce FALLS between 1900 and 1935 (phase 1: 5.36 → 6.45M; F106 6.9M at 1935) and the stale-rung payback exceeds 30 years at 1935 (phase 1: 26.7).
_predictions.P3_world: World GDP at 1935 between 0.90× and 1.30× the vanilla mean, with the rest of the world (world − GBR − India) at or above 0.90× vanilla's (phase 1: 0.74×); Britain no longer bimodal — no run with GBR under £350M unless the world is at 0.9× or above.
_predictions.P4_early: 1837–1860 GDP BELOW vanilla, 0.85–0.95× (the lift's price), and rung-0 building profits at 1840 below vanilla's per level.
_predictions.P5_prices: The four decliners deeper than phase 1's pooled 0.57–0.80 of vanilla at 1935, and at least two more goods below vanilla (tools or clothes); prices in WAGE units below vanilla for every tiered good.
_predictions.P6_tier_choice: Below-best build share under 35% (phase 1 39.2 / 37.9) — flat cost removes the price reason to build the old rung.
_predictions.P7_wall: Row P total within ±5% of vanilla's median; pop-matched ≤ +10%.
_predictions.P8_je: Britain's research-entry completions at phase 1's level (median 26, folded) — the bar is unchanged.

_comparison: phase 2 (canon-je24-a22, sessions 20260909_100930 + 20260909_123746, 10 runs) as the nearest book; phase 1 (canon-je24, 30 runs, F107) and F108's census for the stall rate; vanilla n=16 20260821_131149 as the denominator.
_watch: every run ~5 min in: mod marker, version, this run's error window by position, clock (batch_heartbeat.sh at each wake)
first run: first_run_decomp, je_tally, queue_mix; check rung-0 profits at 1840 against the lift
after run 10: an interim F108-style stall census (world GDP ÷ vanilla mean, GBR at 1935)
post-run: preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS, the ledger with phase 2 as --nb
_cost: 30 × 1836→1936 ≈ 30 × 2h40 ≈ 80 h ≈ 3.3 days continuous, plus resumes; ~140 MB a run.
_caveats: Three levers change at once (rung-0 inputs, cost ladder, ai_value ladder); nothing here separates them — F108 §6 motivates the cost ladder, the user's ruling the other two.

The lift is uniform: at base prices it takes food/textile/furniture to −6%, steel to −8%, glass/tooling/paper to 0% (measured base wage, wage share 0.25); 1836 realised prices sit 5–20% above base in vanilla, which is what keeps them alive until rung 1 exists.
A leftover STOP file kills the first run at 1836 — the previous batch's stop watcher removes it after SCHEDULE DONE; check before launching.
